notes: Existing repository artifacts support paired-acquisition provenance work, but this audit does not infer missing preparation, block, section, batch, workflow, order, or immutable source-event metadata from result archives.

Strongest public crossed preparation/scanner candidate found. The study reports 46 human tissue types, 13 H&E staining conditions on serial sections, seven slide scanners, aligned coordinates, and 91 original WSIs. Same stained sections are imaged across scanners and different staining conditions use serial sections. Stable block IDs, preparation batches, physical scanner device IDs, scan batches, acquisition order, exact section order/distance, and archive-to-source-event bindings remain unverified; factor_nesting_unresolved.

dataset_name: Multi-Scanner Canine Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma Histopathology Dataset
notes: Strong scanner-contrast candidate: 44 samples and the same glass slides digitized on five scanner systems, with local correspondence and file-level MD5 records. It does not provide multiple preparation conditions or matched serial sections. Scanner serial/device identity, scan batches, acquisition order, and block hierarchy are not explicit.

dataset_name: PLISM registered multi-device and staining tiles
notes: Registered 512x512 tile groups span 13 H&E conditions and 13 imaging devices with common coordinates. Useful for low-cost feasibility and correspondence tests, but not a raw-WSI confirmatory package and still lacks verified batch/order/device-provenance fields; factor_nesting_unresolved.

Serial-section registration candidate with H&E and immunohistochemical sections from small tissue-block volumes. Section ordering is explicitly not guaranteed for some series, preparation/stain conditions vary, and scanner reporting varies by subset. It is useful for serial-section methodology but not a clean crossed scanner/preparation design.

dataset_name: Whole slide images of mouse liver serial sections
notes: Open 3 GB registration dataset containing 15 H&E serial sections of mouse liver and small intestine scanned on one VS200. Useful for validating serial-section handling and section-order metadata extraction, but it has one scanner and one stated preparation condition; license and batch/provenance details require confirmation.
